oneLiner: The purest public bet on the 2026 NAND supercycle just told investors the cycle is dead: mid-to-high-teens growth and ~80% gross margins guided through 2030, and the market paid it a 30% three-day rally to start believing.
thesis: AI inference has structurally rewired NAND demand. Server eSSDs were 48% of industry bit shipments in Q2 CY2026; Sandisk datacenter revenue rose 437% in FY2026 and 103% QoQ in Q4, and the QLC Stargate platform began revenue shipments for high-capacity AI data lakes.

The NBM contract model attacks cyclicality head-on. Ten New Business Model agreements worth a minimum $93.9B with 4+ years of visibility have been signed, and management expects NBMs to cover 50%+ of FY2027 bits with locked pricing.

Management now guides the through-cycle. At the Aug 13, 2026 investor day, Sandisk targeted mid-to-high-teens annual revenue growth for 2028-2030 with non-GAAP gross margins around 80%, and said demand outpaces its supply with output tight into 2028.

Supply discipline is holding. Capex stays near 6% of revenue, BiCS8 carries the majority of bit production, BiCS10 production began at Kitakami Fab2 in July 2026, and the Kioxia JV was extended to 2034.
It is a cash machine returning capital. FY2026 GAAP net income was $11.43B on $20.25B revenue, and the buyback authorization was expanded to $15.5B.

latestProse: Q4 FY2026 (reported August 5) was a blowout: revenue of $8.965B rose 51% sequentially and 372% YoY, with roughly one-third of the sequential gain from volume and two-thirds from pricing. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 84.6% against a 79-81% guide, producing non-GAAP EPS of $39.25 (consensus $34.45), and datacenter revenue of $2,977M doubled sequentially to ~33% of sales. Then the Aug 13 investor day reframed the whole debate: CFO Luis Visoso told investors the NAND market passes $300B in 2026 and $500B in 2027, that demand exceeds Sandisk's supply with output tight into 2028, and - with Kioxia - showed a ninth-generation 2Tb QLC part with a 4.8Gb/s interface (+33% vs prior gen) built on CMOS-bonded-array wafer bonding, plus a sampled 1Tb BiCS10 chip with 59% higher bit density. The disclosure that matters most: management formally guided mid-to-high-teens annual revenue growth with ~80% gross margins for 2028 through 2030 - a claim, backed by $93.9B of NBM contracts, that NAND is no longer a cyclical business.
guidanceProse: Q1 FY2027 guidance: revenue $10.3-10.8B, non-GAAP gross margin 83-85%, non-GAAP EPS $44-46 - record numbers that still read as deceleration, since sequential growth is now mostly volume with NBM contracts locking pricing. The investor day then extended the horizon: mid-to-high-teens revenue growth for 2028-2030 at ~80% gross margin, supply tight into 2028, and a technology roadmap (gen-9 2Tb QLC at 4.8Gb/s, BiCS10 in production at Kitakami Fab2 since July) to defend cost leadership. Wall Street cheered - the stock rose roughly 30% across Aug 12-14 to $1,641.11 - but the structure of the debate is unchanged: bulls see contracted, de-cyclicalized economics; bears see peak-cycle margins being extrapolated to 2030 at precisely the moment $500B TAM forecasts invite a supply response.

guide.label: Q1 FY2027 revenue guide
guide.sub: GM 83-85%, EPS $44-46; investor day targets mid-to-high-teens growth at ~80% GM for 2028-2030

segments: Datacenter (enterprise SSD/AI): $2,977M, ~33% of Q4 revenue, +103% QoQ, +437% YoY for FY26 - mix was ~12% entering the fiscal year
Edge (client/mobile/OEM): $5,432M, ~61% of Q4 revenue, +48% QoQ on repricing
Consumer (retail cards/drives): $556M, ~6% and shrinking as bits shift to eSSD
competitive: Q2 CY2026 NAND share by shipments: Samsung 25%, SK Hynix 22%, YMTC 14% (top-3 for the first time), then Kioxia, Micron, and Sandisk sixth by volume - though Sandisk and Kioxia rank higher by revenue on richer eSSD mix
Kioxia is simultaneously JV partner (shared fabs, common BiCS roadmap, JV extended to 2034, joint gen-9 CBA flash) and direct rival in enterprise SSD
Samsung and SK Hynix are diverting capex priority toward HBM/DRAM, a key reason NAND supply stayed tight; their re-entry appetite is the biggest swing factor
YMTC's volume surge is the wildcard supply threat, mitigated for now by its low eSSD share and export-control constraints
moat: NAND is a commodity: no supplier holds pricing power through a full cycle, and today's 84.6% margin is cycle rent, not moat. Sandisk's durable edges are cost/scale via the Kioxia JV and BiCS8/BiCS10 node leadership (with gen-9 CBA wafer bonding), plus - if they hold in a downturn - NBM contracts that convert spot exposure into multi-year committed volumes. The contracts are unproven in a falling-price environment, and the 2028-2030 targets assume they hold.
risks: Peak-cycle margins are unprecedented and now guided to persist. No NAND maker has sustained 80%+ gross margin through a cycle; the investor day made ~80% the official 2028-2030 target, raising the cost of any miss.
Double-ordering risk. Prior shortages ended when customers who double-ordered walked away; a $93.9B 'minimum' backlog built at panic pricing is exactly where that unwinds.

The supply response is coming. YMTC hit 14% shipment share, and management's own $500B CY2027 TAM call is precisely the signal that historically triggers competitor capacity expansion into 2027-28 oversupply.
NBM enforceability is untested. Minimum-value, multi-year agreements have never been through a NAND downturn.
Kioxia JV dependence. Capacity and node-transition decisions are shared, not controlled; BiCS10 and gen-9 CBA execution risk is material.

Expectations just ratcheted higher. A ~30% three-day rally into a $1,641 print leaves consensus FY2027 EPS near $396 as the floor, not the bar; the first soft ASP data point now hits both the E and the multiple.
catalysts: Late Oct/early Nov 2026: Q1 FY2027 earnings - first print against the investor-day framework
Late Oct 2026: Samsung and SK Hynix Q3 CY2026 NAND capex commentary
Nov-Dec 2026: TrendForce/Counterpoint Q3 CY2026 NAND pricing and share data
Ongoing: additional NBM agreements, $15.5B buyback execution, BiCS10/gen-9 CBA ramp milestones
pricedIn: SNDK closed at $1,641.11 on Aug 14, 2026, up roughly 30% in the three sessions around the investor day and up ~7x over the past year, though still ~30% below the early-summer high near $2,350. The forward P/E is roughly 4.1x on consensus FY2027 EPS near $396 - the classic trough-multiple-on-peak-earnings memory setup, now colliding with management guidance that earnings will not trough. Consensus target was near $2,054 (Strong Buy) before the event and targets are migrating higher. The debate: if the 2028-2030 guide (mid-to-high-teens growth, ~80% GM) is even half right, 4x forward is absurdly cheap; if this is a normal cycle wearing contracts as a costume, the market just paid a 30% premium for the costume.

scenarios.bear: The cycle tops in FY2027: supply responds (YMTC, restarted Samsung/SK Hynix NAND capex), customers work down double-ordered inventory, NBM minimums get renegotiated, and ASPs roll; margins fall toward historical 30-40%, EPS collapses to a small fraction of consensus, and the stock overshoots down toward the pre-surge hundreds.
scenarios.base: Shortage conditions persist through CY2027 but pricing flattens; margins ease into the 70s, FY2027 non-GAAP EPS lands meaningfully below the $396 consensus but still very high, and the stock oscillates in the $1,300-1,900 range as the market demands proof the 2028-2030 guide survives a soft quarter.
scenarios.bull: AI storage demand keeps NAND undersupplied into CY2028, the ~$500B CY2027 TAM view proves roughly right, NBM coverage above 50% of bits holds pricing through wobbles, and the 2028-2030 targets start getting modeled as base case; even at 5-6x forward the stock exceeds the pre-event $2,054 consensus target.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings, MU-style: at ~4x forward the market still prices a violent earnings decline - the reverse DCF quantifies the implied annual collapse rate against management's new 2028-2030 growth guide. Only 3 years of standalone filings exist (Feb 2025 spin).
